definitions.meaning: a rider of a motorcycle built for off-road dirt tracks
someone who stirs eggs in a pan while they set, a playful agent-noun

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a motorcyclist on a trail bike; the other jokingly names whoever whisks eggs into a morning dish.

parts.note: viz and sc (scilicet) are both Latin abbreviations meaning 'namely'
to polish is to rub a surface

explanation.surface: Instructions to scour something, that is, give it a good polish.
explanation.walkthrough: SC, short for scilicet, is used in the same way as 'viz', meaning 'namely'.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour a pan is to clean it by hard rubbing, a close synonym.

clue.text: Unwanted animal outside 'ouse, climbing to get up again

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the outside of the second, holding it within

parts.note: a runt is the weakling of a litter, often the animal nobody wants

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the word reads upward, so it is turned back to front

parts.note: house with its H dropped, as a Cockney says it, is (h)ome without the H

explanation.surface: A Cockney story of an unwanted creature scaling the outside of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ouse is Cockney for house, so it is home with its H dropped too; 'climbing' turns that upward, inside a litter's weakling.
explanation.definitionFit: To mount a horse or bike a second time after falling is to climb back on it.

indicators.note: making signals that the following words are worked into something new by rearrangement

explanation.surface: Political pledges before a vote that leave some voters close to swooning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is the anagram signal: SOME and FAINT together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A party's published programme of policies is issued ahead of a vote.

parts.note: the second invention is a made-up story, a falsehood, and the first is a machine built to catch such untruths

explanation.definitionFit: A polygraph is a device devised to detect when someone is telling untruths.

indicators.note: they say means the word is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a rank is a row or line, as of soldiers or seats

explanation.surface: A complaint that some eggs smell off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like an adjective meaning smelly, but it is the noun meaning a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish eggs in a mass are called this, as in cod's caviar-like spawn.

parts.note: a topi is a sun helmet, the pith helmet of colonial days
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone complains their hat leaves them chilly, and that is what matters.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject or matter under discussion is an issue.

parts.note: taken as written
a pup is a baby dog or seal

explanation.surface: A fresh bottle handed to an infant.
explanation.definitionFit: A further helping that fills a glass back to the brim.

indicators.note: holds means the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: a kitty is a pool of money, a pot in cards

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: dire means horrible or dreadful

explanation.surface: A cat clutching an ugly rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the word for horrible back to front, and 'holds' puts it inside the pot. 'Kitty' looks like a cat but is a betting pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A peridot is an olive-green gemstone, a precious mineral.

parts.note: a crew from the city of Cork might be called by the possessive of that city plus crew, and the phrase is also a bottle-opening tool

explanation.walkthrough: Cork is a city in the Republic of Ireland; read the answer as that city's crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiral metal tool for pulling stoppers from wine bottles opens them.

clue.text: Italian church — some say it's dead

parts.note: a Roman is an Italian from Rome
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An Italian church that some people claim is no longer living.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic hint: people often lament that love and courtship are dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Courtship and love affairs are the thing people complain no longer exists.

clue.text: Japanese version of the king penguin

definitions.meaning: Japan's monarch is styled with a title above king
the largest species of penguin, from Antarctica

explanation.definitionFit: Japan's sovereign is given this imperial title, and it also names the biggest Antarctic penguin.

definitions.meaning: frank and hearty in a good-natured way
a pretence intended to mislead, as in poker

explanation.definitionFit: A bluff manner is genially outspoken; and a bluff in cards is a feint to deceive.

clue.text: Greek dramatist, regret rejected, I spied in ruins

indicators.note: rejected means the word is thrown back, so read in reverse

parts.note: to rue is to regret
taken as written

indicators.note: in ruins signals that the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A Greek playwright, with regret, rejected, glimpsed among ancient ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text runs 'Greekdramatist' together and has lost the I before 'spied'; the wordplay needs it. Rue means regret; 'rejected' turns it back, and 'in ruins' scrambles SPIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Euripides was one of the three great tragic playwrights of ancient Athens.

parts.note: red-hot means very sexy or passionate
poker is a card game

explanation.surface: A steamy game played in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' suggests the bedroom, but it is a flower bed: this is a tall garden plant with flaming spikes.
explanation.definitionFit: Kniphofia, a garden perennial with torch-like spikes, grows in a flower bed.

clue.text: Biblical character left — where would you find him?

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is where this figure appears

explanation.surface: A question about where to locate a biblical figure who has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Lot, Abraham's nephew whose wife turned to salt, appears in Genesis, in the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Lot is a figure from Genesis, the nephew of Abraham who fled Sodom.

parts.note: the proverb says one final piece of chaff added to the load breaks the camel's back, and camels carry goods across Africa

explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial final addition that makes a burden unbearable, from the camel's broken back.

indicators.note: adjusted signals that the letters are altered into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A dial set further back in the dashboard, then adjusted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusted' is the anagram signal for MORE and DEEP-SET together.
explanation.definitionFit: A dashboard instrument that measures and displays how fast a vehicle goes.

clue.text: Item worth being renovated-that's common sense

indicators.note: being renovated says the letters are rebuilt into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Restoring an object of value is the sensible thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being renovated' rearranges ITEM and WORTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Native wit or practical good judgement one is born with is plain sense.

clue.text: Fish hiding after day in marine compound

indicators.note: after says the defeat comes behind the other assembled piece
in means the day sits inside the compound

parts.note: salt, sodium chloride, is the compound in seawater
MON is short for Monday
a hiding is a thrashing, a rout or heavy defeat

explanation.surface: A fish taking cover after a day spent in some sea chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' looks like concealment but means a thrashing, ROUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea trout, a migratory brown trout, is a species of game fish.

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the first piece circles the second

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A politician on tour in Ireland, giving lustful looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a parliamentarian, but it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Leering describes eyeing someone with a lustful, suggestive look.

clue.text: Fruit tart for sale, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is heard spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: a tart for sale is a prostitute

explanation.surface: A fruit tart offered for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' looks like a pastry but is slang for a prostitute; in non-rhotic British speech the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The red berry of the hawthorn bush is a small fruit.

parts.note: a hem is the border of a garment
a lock provides security

explanation.surface: A poison used to secure a boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: A toxic plant whose extract killed Socrates.

clue.text: Drug taken with gin, the curse of drivers?

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
a gin is a snare or trap for game

explanation.surface: Amphetamine mixed with gin, a menace to motorists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' suggests the spirit, but it is a hunter's snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A radar check that catches motorists exceeding the limit is hated by them.

parts.note: the rear is the bottom or backside

explanation.surface: A gloomy moment when a daughter shows her backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a literary word for dismal and gloomy.

indicators.note: appearing in says the letters show up within the run of the following words

explanation.surface: An insect turning up in a song, figuratively speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across anthEM METaphorically.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmet is an old dialect word for this small insect.

clue.text: Speaking of fish, the piano man?

indicators.note: speaking of says the word is spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: tuna is a large sea fish

explanation.surface: An aside about fish and a pianist.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the fish and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano tuner adjusts the instrument's strings to pitch.

clue.text: Point cuts through tear in clothing

indicators.note: cuts through means the first piece is placed inside the second

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip
to aim is to point

explanation.surface: A sharp point slicing through a rip in a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an archaic word for clothes and garments.

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word, starting with the first

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer and also builds it from alternate letters of 'Twitch'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tic is an involuntary spasm that recurs habitually.

clue.text: Hooter breaks recess, then recalled in eastern peninsula

indicators.note: breaks means the first piece cuts into the other
recalled means called back, so read in reverse

parts.note: a nook is a recess or alcove
an owl hoots, so it is a hooter

explanation.surface: A horn breaks a quiet corner, then is called back, in an Asian peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns the recess back to front and 'breaks' puts the bird inside it. Kowloon is the mainland peninsula of Hong Kong.
explanation.definitionFit: Kowloon is the mainland peninsula facing Hong Kong Island, in East Asia.

indicators.note: nameless means without N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: Wagner was a German composer of operas

explanation.surface: A bet that a composer will turn up anonymously.
explanation.definitionFit: A wager is a stake or bet placed on an outcome.

clue.text: School worker, perhaps, given further test in vehicle

indicators.note: in means placed inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a retake is a resit of an exam

explanation.surface: A school employee given another exam in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: A school janitor is the example; 'perhaps' signals that.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitor who looks after a building is one example of this role.
